text.title: Trend Analysis Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on when the consuming decision executes, whether independent published series exist in the domain, and how fast those series move relative to the review cycle — to a full 12-24 month scan, a sourcing fix, a per-trend expiry regime, or a skip.

decision-tree.root-question: When does the decision this scan feeds actually execute, and is it a decision at all?

branch.when: the decision executes inside the current quarter

conclusion.verdict: skip: a 12-24 month read cannot change a decision that lands this quarter — route to market-analysis for a current-state view

branch.when: the output is narrative for a pitch, a deck or a keynote rather than an input to a decision

conclusion.verdict: skip: the fields would be filled with plausible fiction and then quoted with the authority of the format

branch.when: the decision executes 12-24 months out, or sets a direction over that horizon
branch.question: What does the evidence base for this domain actually consist of?

branch.when: opinion pieces and analyst commentary only; nobody publishes a repeated series in the domain

conclusion.verdict: skip: `three-signals-not-three-citations-of-one` cannot be satisfied, so `signals_per_trend` could only be filled with fiction

branch.when: several outlets cover it, but every citation traces back to one analyst report or one vendor dataset

conclusion.verdict: widen sourcing before drafting: three signals with genuinely independent primary sources per trend, at least one a hard series — price, volume, headcount, filings, procurement or regulatory calendar

branch.when: the candidates are written as directional statements — adoption is accelerating, interest is growing — with no metric and no two dated values

conclusion.verdict: convert or cut: each entry needs a metric, a t0 value with date, a t1 value with date and the series source; what survives as a direction only is a theme and leaves the artefact

branch.when: the only quantitative source is an annual survey whose field window closed months before publication

conclusion.verdict: add at least one higher-frequency leading indicator before claiming a 12-month horizon, and record field date separately from publication date on every signal

branch.when: at least three independent primary sources per candidate trend, one of them a hard series with dated t0 and t1 values

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology: measured rates, per-trend expiry, a pre-committed disconfirmer, and implications that name the decision and its direction

branch.when: series exist but the domain re-prints them faster than the cycle that would refresh this artefact
branch.question: Can each trend carry a re-measurement date you would actually honour?

branch.when: the fastest series re-prints more often than the shortest `valid_until` the team could realistically act on

conclusion.verdict: skip: a periodic scan is structurally stale here — set up continuous monitoring against the series instead

branch.when: the direction is already treated as settled internally and nobody has named an observation that would change their mind

conclusion.verdict: fix the disconfirmer at authoring time: a specific metric, a threshold and where it is published, per trend, and never rewritten at review to fit what happened

branch.when: series move at different speeds and each can carry its own re-measurement date inside the horizon

conclusion.verdict: run the scan with per-trend `valid_until` set shorter than `horizon_months` for the fast series; cite nothing past its own expiry
